page: Microsoft Azure F48ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core ratio without simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 192 GB of RAM, allocating 4 GB per physical core. For high-speed temporary I/O, the instance bundles 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside support for Premium Storage. Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512 vector extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration flags such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution speed across dense compute and memory tasks. In stress-ng testing, single-core throughput scored 3,790.09 and multi-core reached 176,118.25, placing the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Geekbench metrics reinforce this profile with a 2,862.0 single-core score, a 29,245.0 multi-core score, and a clang software compilation score of 74,261.0. Read bandwidth for cached small blocks reaches 9,372.72 GB/sec, while uncached large-block write operations sustained 170.75 GB/sec. The instance also achieved 135.87 million operations per second in Redis SET testing.

The 1:1 mapping of 48 vCPUs to 48 dedicated physical cores ensures deterministic execution times free from hyperthreading contention. While lacking discrete GPU hardware, the integrated AVX-512 extensions provide capable small-to-medium CPU-based LLM inference, sustaining 5,492.85 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model and 56.24 tokens per second text generation on a 7B model. However, performance tapers on larger 70B parameter models.

The inclusion of 5.6 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with high computational density makes the F48ads_v7 well suited for distributed build pipelines, large-scale Clang compilations, high-throughput in-memory datastores, batch video and image processing, and heavy analytical database operations.
description: Microsoft Azure F48ads_v7 is a compute-optimized instance driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz across 48 dedicated physical cores without multithreading. Equipped with 192 GB of system memory and 5,670 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, the instance is engineered for deterministic, high-throughput workloads. Supported hardware vector extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 instructions. In benchmark testing, the F48ads_v7 demonstrates top-decile performance in multi-core stress execution, software compilation, and in-memory operations, recording 135.87 million Redis SET operations per second and 687.11 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The combination of dedicated physical cores and extensive local NVMe capacity delivers high computational and storage efficiency for tasks lacking GPU requirements, making the instance optimal for database workloads, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, and high-frequency data processing pipelines.
